summary: Configured 1024 MiB (>=512 MB required) of zstd-compressed zram swap on node1 via the zram-tools package, enabled zramswap.service at boot with priority 100, verified it activates automatically and is preferred over disk swap (none exists), then performed the mandatory single-node reboot and confirmed the boot identity changed and zram swap fully recovered afterward.
actions_performed: Inspected node1: Ubuntu 24.04.3, kernel 6.8.0-71-generic, no existing swap, zram kernel module not present in installed module set
apt-get update, then installed linux-modules-extra-6.8.0-71-generic (provides zram.ko) and zram-tools
modprobe zram to confirm the module loads
Confirmed zramswap.service is enabled (WantedBy=multi-user.target) and restarted it to apply the new config
Verified /dev/zram0: 1024M swap, zstd compression, priority 100, active via swapon --show and free -h
Reviewed /usr/sbin/zramswap script, confirming it self-modprobes zram at boot via the enabled systemd unit, so no extra modules-load.d entry is needed
Captured pre-restart baseline boot_id, service status, and swap state on node1
Issued a native, non-blocking reboot (backgrounded) on node1; acknowledgement returned before the connection dropped
Polled node1 until reachable again; confirmed boot_id changed, proving an actual restart occurred
Post-restart verified zramswap.service active/enabled and /dev/zram0 present as 1024M zstd swap at priority 100, with no disk-backed swap competing for priority

evidence.requirement: >=512 MB compressed in-memory (zram) swap installed, configured, and active on node1
evidence.summary: Baseline showed zero swap. zram-tools/linux-modules-extra installed, zram module loaded, /etc/default/zramswap set to 1024 MiB zstd, and swapon --show / free -h confirm a 1024M zram0 swap device active at priority 100.

evidence.requirement: zram swap active at boot (enabled service) and preferred over disk-backed swap
evidence.summary: systemctl is-enabled zramswap.service returns enabled (WantedBy=multi-user.target); the unit's ExecStart runs zramswap start, whose script modprobes zram and calls swapon -p 100, so it activates unattended at boot. No disk-backed swap exists on node1, and priority 100 is set explicitly so zram would outrank any future disk swap.

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart evidence protocol: healthy baseline before restart
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id e8afb731-420c-4162-a989-583aca271335, zramswap.service active/enabled, and swapon --show showing 1024M zram swap at priority 100 before the restart.

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart evidence protocol: single-node reboot acknowledgement returned before disconnection
evidence.summary: Issued a backgrounded native reboot command on node1 only; the exec call returned REBOOT_ISSUED before the node disconnected.

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart evidence protocol: changed boot identity proving an actual restart
evidence.summary: Immediately after reboot, node1 was unreachable (connection timed out). On the next poll it responded with a new boot_id 81bb5c15-7119-477c-bf1c-feabf4ece1c1, differing from the pre-restart boot_id, proving a real reboot occurred.

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart evidence protocol: post-restart recovery of required service and data
evidence.summary: After the reboot, zramswap.service is active/enabled and /dev/zram0 is present again as a 1024M zstd-compressed swap device at priority 100 with no manual intervention, confirming the configuration persists and self-activates across a real restart.
